# DESIGN — Event Contract v0 (the fleet's published language)

Tracking: [JES-128](https://linear.app/honeycombio/issue/JES-128) · Status: **draft v2, incorporating Jess's first commentary round** (round 1 is in git history)

The language-neutral event contract the Spine publishes and both TS apps validate
against. Will become JSON Schema in `contracts/` at the repo root; this doc is where
we make the decisions first. Leave comments inline — each decision is numbered.

Guiding constraints (from SEAMAP.md / the vision doc, as amended by round 1):

- One append-only event log per Table. Never replace — supersede.
- Visibility on every event. **The shadow is a first-class event**: the private fact
  it shadows may never reach the Spine at all (the Shuffler keeps hands and libraries
  to itself and sends only the public shadow of what it knows). Visibility marks what
  an event reveals, not a derivation chain.
- **Provenance and observability are separate.** Provenance is on the event itself —
  who initiated it, which app recorded it, when — and is durable. Trace context is
  recorded too (super useful for seeing the connections right now) but expires in
  60d, so nothing auditable may depend on it. Durable causality between events uses
  event `id` references, never trace ids.
- Versioned from the start; old data fails loudly. Accepted consequence today: a
  deploy can invalidate a Table. If this ever becomes publicly useful, backwards
  compatibility must hold for at least the length of a game.
- Not all events are game events — see Decision 6 (scope).
- **The developer can see the log**: the Spine includes an admin screen (a webapp
  component is fine) that shows a table's log human-readably, linking each event to
  its trace in Honeycomb. (Scoped into JES-129.)

---

## Card Identity — an important concept, named

How a card is serialized in any event payload, ever:

- **Identity is the Scryfall ID.** It captures the exact printing: oracle identity,
  all faces, all names (oracle name and the vanity/flavor name), all image URIs.
- **Face is card state, not identity** — but it matters at play time (MDFCs are
  played as a chosen face), so events about playing/revealing a card carry
  `face` alongside identity. The Shuffler already tracks `currentFace`; it must
  send it.
- Names and image URLs are *derivable conveniences*, not identity, and don't belong
  in the contract's card reference. (The pre-Spine Shuffler→Tabletop scaffolding API
  may carry an `imageUrl` for rendering without a Scryfall lookup — that's the
  scaffolding's business, not the contract's.)

Contract shape: `card: { scryfallId }` + sibling `face` where the event needs it.

## Decision 1: The envelope — v2, renames from round 1 applied

| field | who writes it | what it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | **sender** mints a GUID | idempotency — the Spine elides a retried duplicate |
| `tableId` | sender (after learning it) | which table's log. A GUID the **Spine mints at table creation** — the table *name* is a lookup alias, unique only among active tables, living in the `table.created` payload. **PROPOSED, needs your yes** |
| `seq` | **Spine**, on append | authoritative order within the log; senders cannot claim positions |
| `name` | sender | the event's kind, namespaced (`card.played`); determines the payload schema. See Decision 6 |
| `scope` | sender | what the event affects / how it's perceived — see Decision 6, OPEN |
| `acceptedAt` | **Spine**, on append | Spine's clock: when the log accepted it |
| `occurredAt` | sender, optional | the initiator app's clock, when physics preceded ingestion |
| `initiator` | sender | *who* made this happen: a seat, a named spectator, later the interpreter |
| `occurredIn` | sender | *which application* recorded/sent it: `shuffler`, `tabletop`, `spine`, later `interpreter` |
| `visibility` | sender | `public` — the only legal value in v0; see Decision 4 |
| `traceparent` | sender | W3C trace context — **observability only**, expires with the trace (60d); the admin screen links through it to Honeycomb |
| `schemaVersion` | sender | integer version of this `name`'s payload schema |
| `payload` | sender | the kind-specific body |

**The split in one line:** uniqueness travels with the event (sender GUID);
truth-of-order and truth-of-time stay with the log (Spine-assigned `seq`,
`acceptedAt`).

## Decision 2: The v0 event catalog — OPEN, firming up

- `table.created` — payload: table name, creator. Response/log carries the minted `tableId`.
- `seat.taken` — payload: seat number (1–4), player name
- `card.played` — from the Shuffler (Decision 3: **decided, game event**) —
  payload: `card: { scryfallId }`, `face`, from which seat, zone hint

Near-future, not v0: the Tabletop reporting the *physical* echo (`card.arrived`,
scope visible) once it talks to the Spine — mostly ignored by interpretation because
it's expected; **interesting precisely when it doesn't arrive**. Also not v0: card
movement/tap, chat, interpretation events. Kinds arrive when their producers do.

## Decision 3: Game event vs. physical — DECIDED: (a) game event

The Shuffler is a deterministic, not-interpreted app: when it plays a card it knows
the meaning, so it says so — `card.played`, scope `game`. Physical events are
reserved for genuinely observed/ambiguous happenings (the Tabletop's world), and the
physical echo of a game event is a separate, expected, low-drama event (see
Decision 2). This seeds the log with ground-truth game events for the Interpreter's
eval dataset.

## Decision 4: Visibility — RESOLVED for v0: everything is `public`

Answering round 1's question directly: **no, the Spine does not receive seat-private
events in v0** — the Shuffler was never going to send both halves of a pair; it
sends only the public shadow of what it privately knows ("seat 2 drew a card",
never which card). So v0's enum is exactly `public`, and the pair/shadow mechanics
are deferred until a producer actually wants to log a private fact. Envelope
future-proofing kept: when shadows arrive, a shadow references the `id` of the event
it shadows; adding an enum value is an envelope version bump that old readers reject
loudly. (Whether the Spine *ever* holds seat-private facts is a real future
decision, not assumed.)

## Decision 5: Versioning mechanics — DECIDED

- Each event `name` versions its payload schema independently (`schemaVersion: 1`
  under `name: seat.taken`).
- The envelope itself carries one version (file-level in `contracts/`), bumped
  rarely.
- Both readers validate on receipt and **fail loudly** on unknown name or version —
  consistent with `notes/DESIGN-persistence-versioning.md`.

Where TS receives events: eventually the **Tabletop subscribes to a table's public
feed** from the Spine — it needs `card.played` to put things on the stack — and that
subscription is where TS-side contract validation lives. (In v0's scaffolding the
Shuffler POSTs to the Tabletop directly; the code carries `// JES-128` markers where
validation will land.)

## Decision 6 (new, from round 1): `name` + `scope` are separate fields — OPEN

Round 1's insight: filtering wants a dimension that payload-schema naming doesn't
give. You'd filter by *what the event affects / how it's perceived*: affects the
table; affects the game; is visible; is audible (conceptually including chat).
Proposal to react to:

- `name` — determines the payload schema, namespaced for humans: `card.played`,
  `card.moved`, `seat.taken`, `chat.said`
- `scope` — one of `table` | `game` | `visible` | `audible` (bikeshed welcome:
  is a chat message `audible`? is a sticky note `visible`?)

Open sub-questions: is scope exactly one value or could an event carry several
(a spoken "I attack" is audible *and* affects the game)? Does the Interpreter's
output (`interpretation.*`) get its own scope or is it `game`?

## Not decided here (future docs)

- Supersession/correction event shapes (Interpreter era) — durable causality via
  event `id` references (`supersedes:`, `evidence:`), per the provenance constraint.
- Chat events, transcription events.
- Projections (current reading, public view, narration feed) — Spine internals, not
  contract. (The admin screen is a projection consumer.)
- Transport (HTTP POST vs websocket) — contract is transport-neutral.

# DESIGN — Event Contract v0 (the fleet's published language)

Tracking: [JES-128](https://linear.app/honeycombio/issue/JES-128) · Status: **draft v2, incorporating Jess's first commentary round** (round 1 is in git history)

The language-neutral event contract the Spine publishes and both TS apps validate
against. Will become JSON Schema in `contracts/` at the repo root; this doc is where
we make the decisions first. Leave comments inline — each decision is numbered.

Guiding constraints (from SEAMAP.md / the vision doc, as amended by round 1):

- One append-only event log per Table. Never replace — supersede.
- Visibility on every event. **The shadow is a first-class event**: the private fact
  it shadows may never reach the Spine at all (the Shuffler keeps hands and libraries
  to itself and sends only the public shadow of what it knows). Visibility marks what
  an event reveals, not a derivation chain.
- **Provenance and observability are separate.** Provenance is on the event itself —
  who initiated it, which app recorded it, when — and is durable. Trace context is
  recorded too (super useful for seeing the connections right now) but expires in
  60d, so nothing auditable may depend on it. Durable causality between events uses
  event `id` references, never trace ids.
- Versioned from the start; old data fails loudly. Accepted consequence today: a
  deploy can invalidate a Table. If this ever becomes publicly useful, backwards
  compatibility must hold for at least the length of a game.
- Not all events are game events — see Decision 6 (scope).
- **The developer can see the log**: the Spine includes an admin screen (a webapp
  component is fine) that shows a table's log human-readably, linking each event to
  its trace in Honeycomb. (Scoped into JES-129.)

---

## Card Identity — an important concept, named

How a card is serialized in any event payload, ever:

- **Identity is the Scryfall ID.** It captures the exact printing: oracle identity,
  all faces, all names (oracle name and the vanity/flavor name), all image URIs.
- **Face is card state, not identity** — but it matters at play time (MDFCs are
  played as a chosen face), so events about playing/revealing a card carry
  `face` alongside identity. The Shuffler already tracks `currentFace`; it must
  send it.
- Names and image URLs are *derivable conveniences*, not identity, and don't belong
  in the contract's card reference. (The pre-Spine Shuffler→Tabletop scaffolding API
  may carry an `imageUrl` for rendering without a Scryfall lookup — that's the
  scaffolding's business, not the contract's.)

**Identity has two levels** (round 2): the *definition* and the *instance*.

- **Definition** — `scryfallId`, as above: what kind of card this is.
- **Instance** — `cardInstanceId`: *this particular Forest*, the way a physical deck
  has one. A GUID minted by the Shuffler, one per card, when the deck becomes a
  game's library. Game-mechanically two Forests are equivalent; log-wise they are
  distinct individuals, so a single card can be followed through played → tapped →
  sacrificed → graveyard, and conservation of cards is checkable: if the table ever
  holds more or fewer Forests than the log accounts for, each instance's event
  biography shows exactly where. (The Shuffler's internal `gameCardIndex` is the
  embryo of this — it *is* static for the life of a game, but it's assigned after
  sorting the deck alphabetically (`GameState.newGame`), so an index is the card's
  alphabetical rank in a known decklist: **a decodable secret**. It must never cross
  the Shuffler's boundary; the contract gets an opaque GUID instead.)
- Minting scope, decided-unless-vetoed: **per game**, at game start. "Same physical
  card across game nights" (persisting instance ids into deck files) is a noted
  future upgrade, fragile today because deck files are regenerated from
  Archidekt/MTGJSON.

Contract shape: `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }` + sibling `face` where the event
needs it. Downstream consequence: the Tabletop should stamp `instanceId` into each
card shape's `meta`, so future physical events (`card.moved`, tap) reference the
same individual the game events do.

## Decision 1: The envelope — v2, renames from round 1 applied

| field | who writes it | what it's for |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | **sender** mints a GUID | idempotency — the Spine elides a retried duplicate |
| `tableId` | sender (after learning it) | which table's log. A GUID the **Spine mints at table creation** — the table *name* is a lookup alias, unique only among active tables, living in the `table.created` payload. **PROPOSED, needs your yes** |
| `seq` | **Spine**, on append | authoritative order within the log; senders cannot claim positions |
| `name` | sender | the event's kind, namespaced (`card.played`); determines the payload schema. See Decision 6 |
| `scope` | sender | what the event affects / how it's perceived — see Decision 6, OPEN |
| `acceptedAt` | **Spine**, on append | Spine's clock: when the log accepted it |
| `occurredAt` | sender, optional | the initiator app's clock, when physics preceded ingestion |
| `initiator` | sender | *who* made this happen: a seat, a named spectator, later the interpreter |
| `occurredIn` | sender | *which application* recorded/sent it: `shuffler`, `tabletop`, `spine`, later `interpreter` |
| `visibility` | sender | `public` — the only legal value in v0; see Decision 4 |
| `traceparent` | sender | W3C trace context — **observability only**, expires with the trace (60d); the admin screen links through it to Honeycomb |
| `schemaVersion` | sender | integer version of this `name`'s payload schema |
| `payload` | sender | the kind-specific body |

**The split in one line:** uniqueness travels with the event (sender GUID);
truth-of-order and truth-of-time stay with the log (Spine-assigned `seq`,
`acceptedAt`).

## Decision 2: The v0 event catalog — OPEN, firming up

- `table.created` — payload: table name, creator. Response/log carries the minted `tableId`.
- `seat.taken` — payload: seat number (1–4), player name
- `card.played` — from the Shuffler (Decision 3: **decided, game event**) —
  payload: `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }`, `face`, from which seat, zone hint

Near-future, not v0: the Tabletop reporting the *physical* echo (`card.arrived`,
scope visible) once it talks to the Spine — mostly ignored by interpretation because
it's expected; **interesting precisely when it doesn't arrive**. Also not v0: card
movement/tap, chat, interpretation events. Kinds arrive when their producers do.

## Decision 3: Game event vs. physical — DECIDED: (a) game event

The Shuffler is a deterministic, not-interpreted app: when it plays a card it knows
the meaning, so it says so — `card.played`, scope `game`. Physical events are
reserved for genuinely observed/ambiguous happenings (the Tabletop's world), and the
physical echo of a game event is a separate, expected, low-drama event (see
Decision 2). This seeds the log with ground-truth game events for the Interpreter's
eval dataset.

## Decision 4: Visibility — RESOLVED for v0: everything is `public`

Answering round 1's question directly: **no, the Spine does not receive seat-private
events in v0** — the Shuffler was never going to send both halves of a pair; it
sends only the public shadow of what it privately knows ("seat 2 drew a card",
never which card). So v0's enum is exactly `public`, and the pair/shadow mechanics
are deferred until a producer actually wants to log a private fact. Envelope
future-proofing kept: when shadows arrive, a shadow references the `id` of the event
it shadows; adding an enum value is an envelope version bump that old readers reject
loudly. (Whether the Spine *ever* holds seat-private facts is a real future
decision, not assumed.)

## Decision 5: Versioning mechanics — DECIDED

- Each event `name` versions its payload schema independently (`schemaVersion: 1`
  under `name: seat.taken`).
- The envelope itself carries one version (file-level in `contracts/`), bumped
  rarely.
- Both readers validate on receipt and **fail loudly** on unknown name or version —
  consistent with `notes/DESIGN-persistence-versioning.md`.

Where TS receives events: eventually the **Tabletop subscribes to a table's public
feed** from the Spine — it needs `card.played` to put things on the stack — and that
subscription is where TS-side contract validation lives. (In v0's scaffolding the
Shuffler POSTs to the Tabletop directly; the code carries `// JES-128` markers where
validation will land.)

## Decision 6 (new, from round 1): `name` + `scope` are separate fields — OPEN

Round 1's insight: filtering wants a dimension that payload-schema naming doesn't
give. You'd filter by *what the event affects / how it's perceived*: affects the
table; affects the game; is visible; is audible (conceptually including chat).
Proposal to react to:

- `name` — determines the payload schema, namespaced for humans: `card.played`,
  `card.moved`, `seat.taken`, `chat.said`
- `scope` — one of `table` | `game` | `visible` | `audible` (bikeshed welcome:
  is a chat message `audible`? is a sticky note `visible`?)

Open sub-questions: is scope exactly one value or could an event carry several
(a spoken "I attack" is audible *and* affects the game)? Does the Interpreter's
output (`interpretation.*`) get its own scope or is it `game`?

## Not decided here (future docs)

- Supersession/correction event shapes (Interpreter era) — durable causality via
  event `id` references (`supersedes:`, `evidence:`), per the provenance constraint.
- Chat events, transcription events.
- Projections (current reading, public view, narration feed) — Spine internals, not
  contract. (The admin screen is a projection consumer.)
- Transport (HTTP POST vs websocket) — contract is transport-neutral.

# PLAN — Tabletop v0 (JES-127)

Planning agent + Jess, two rounds (round-1 commentary is in git history at `56fe5b3`).
Status: **v2 — Jess's round-1 answers folded in; 5 new JESS TODOs at the bottom.**

## Modes (a thing we hadn't named)

- **Solo (default)** — no table name. Play/Discard copy the card image to the
  clipboard; play in Mural or wherever. Today's behavior, unchanged.
- **At a table** — table name + player name entered on the Prep screen. Play/Discard
  send the card to `/t/:tableName`; no clipboard.
- **Spectating** — open `/t/:tableName` with no Shuffler game at all. Full canvas
  access in v0 (no seat concept).

Mirror this into `apps/tabletop/README.md`, `notes/GLOSSARY.md`, and prep-screen copy.

## Technology choices

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Canvas | `tldraw` (v3.x) React component | mandated; watermark worn happily |
| Sync | `@tldraw/sync` (`useSync`) client + self-hosted `@tldraw/sync-core` (`TLSocketRoom`) server on Node + `ws` | hosted demo server can't take server-side shape injection or our OTel; self-hosting is the documented production path |
| Server frame | One Node/Express process: Vite-built static app, `/connect/:roomId` websocket, `POST /api/tables/:tableName/cards`, OTLP proxy, `/health` | one container; sync server stays deliberately dumb |
| Build | Vite + React + TypeScript | standard for a tldraw app |
| Card rendering v0 | tldraw image shape + `TLImageAsset`, `src` = Scryfall URL of the **played face**. `shape.meta` = `{ instanceId, scryfallId, cardName }` — **no traceparent** (traces follow requests; cards persist; correlation is by `card.instance_id` span attribute) | Scryfall scans' round corners are physically-round-things, style-legal. Sleeves/rectangles arrive with the custom CardShape (Mountain 2) — buoy dropped, not accelerated |
| Room registry | in-memory `Map<slug(tableName), { tableId, room: TLSocketRoom }>` — name is the alias, id is the identity (contract Decision 1). **SCAFFOLDING**: the Spine absorbs table identity later | JESS TODO 1: may the scaffolding mint interim tableId GUIDs? |
| Dedup | on event `id` (retry of the request) **and** on `instanceId`-already-on-table (retry of the play — a second arrival of an instance is a physical no-op) | covers the worked-but-unacked case |
| Browser OTel | **standard OTel web SDK** (`@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-web` etc.) wrapped in our own `src/client/observability/` module (`initTracing`, `inSpan`, `setGlobalAttrs`); nothing Honeycomb-specific; spans proxied through our server (`POST /otlp/v1/traces`, key stays server-side — JESS TODO 5); dataset `mtg-tabletop-web` | Jess: standard library, our own wrapper module |
| Unit tests | Vitest for the tabletop (Jess: "no coupling"); Shuffler stays Jest | |

## F — fleet-level steps (first; they unblock A ∥ B parallelism)

- **F0. Freeze the card-arrival payload** — envelope-lite subset of the contract:
  `{ id, name: "card.played", occurredAt, initiator, card: { scryfallId, instanceId }, face, zoneHint: "stack"|"battlefield"|"graveyard", imageUrl, cardName }`
  (`imageUrl`/`cardName` are blessed scaffolding conveniences, not contract).
  **`gameCardIndex` is forbidden beyond the Shuffler's boundary** — it's alphabetical
  rank in a known decklist, a decodable secret. Record the payload as a comment block
  in `apps/shuffler/src/port-tabletop/types.ts` and the tabletop route, both with
  `// JES-128` markers; a unit test asserts the fake gateway never receives an index.
- **F1. Promote the two-faced-cards owner to fleet scope** (before A5, which renders
  a chosen face): restructure `notes/features/two-faced-cards/` into a top-level
  charge ("a card has faces; face is state, not identity") with per-component
  sections — Shuffler (existing), Tabletop (arrival renders the played face; future
  flip gesture), Contract (`face` beside `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }`). Update
  the three `.claude/skills/two-faced-cards-*` triggers. Use the owner's `-update`
  skill per `notes/features/HOW-TO-CREATE-A-FEATURE-OWNER.md`.

## Part A — apps/tabletop (parallel with Part B once F0 lands)

- **A1. Scaffold the workspace** — package.json (tldraw, @tldraw/sync{,-core},
  express, ws, react, OTel), tsconfig, vite.config, src/client + src/server; root
  pass-through scripts. *Test: build compiles, vitest smoke.* **First task: verify
  server-side shape injection (`room.updateStore`) against the pinned tldraw version.**
- **A2. OTel from the first commit** — server: `src/server/tracing.ts` modeled on the
  Shuffler's (ESM register hook, OTLP http, kube-probe-aware sampler, `node --import`).
  Browser: the `observability/` wrapper module (standard OTel web SDK), initialized
  before mount, `table.name` as a global attr; spans go to our server's OTLP proxy.
  `run` script + `.env` pattern (`.be` before `.env` — same trap). *Test: spans in
  Honeycomb env `local`, datasets `mtg-tabletop` / `mtg-tabletop-web`.*
- **A3. Sync server + room registry (scaffolding)** — `rooms.ts` per the registry
  row above; Express + ws upgrade at `/connect/:roomSlug` (accept `traceparent` on
  the connection URL — propagation belongs to the connection *request* only); SPA
  fallback for `/t/*`; `/health`. One shared slugify. Rooms ephemeral, in-memory
  only — accepted for v0 (buoy: durable reconstruction later — card locations
  replayable from the Spine's log once it exists; doodles need a tldraw snapshot
  store). `table.id` + `table.name` on spans. *Test: vitest, real server on an
  ephemeral port, two ws clients share a room.*
- **A4. The `/t/:tableName` page** — `/` landing takes a table name only (player
  name is a Shuffler-prep concern); `/t/:tableName` renders `<Tldraw>` with
  `useSync`. Spectators come free. Square corners, tablet-friendly. *Test:
  Playwright, two contexts, draw in one, see it in the other; tabletop `verify.sh`.*
- **A5. Card-arrival API — the seam the Spine absorbs** — `POST
  /api/tables/:tableName/cards`, payload per F0. Dedup on `id` and on `instanceId`
  already on the table (no-op). **Arrival layout**: a fixed **Stack area**, plus a
  **battlefield row per player** keyed by `initiator` (allocated in first-play
  order); `zoneHint` picks between them (the Shuffler knows land vs nonland from
  `cardTypes`; the tabletop stays meaning-free and just honors coordinates).
  Graveyard placement: JESS TODO 3. `shape.meta` = `{ instanceId, scryfallId,
  cardName }`. Ingestion span carries `card.instance_id`, `card.scryfall_id`,
  `card.name`, `event.id`, `table.name`, `zone.hint`; the client store-listener
  emits a standalone "card arrived on canvas" span correlated by `card.instance_id`
  attribute (not propagation). SCAFFOLDING banner naming the future shape: Shuffler
  emits `card.played` to the Spine; Tabletop subscribes to the table's public feed.
  *Test: vitest POST + both dedup paths; Playwright land vs nonland land in
  different areas.*
- **A6. Docker, k8s, deploy** — Dockerfile with repo root as build context; `k8s/`
  deployment (`mtg-tabletop`, key from `mtg-deck-shuffler-secret`), service, ingress
  on ALB group `only-one-alb-please`, host **`table.jessitron.honeydemo.io`**
  (decided: copy the Shuffler's external-dns + TLS host block; spares Vite base-path
  and ws-path juggling). The Shuffler's server-side POST uses in-cluster DNS
  (`TABLETOP_URL=http://mtg-tabletop-service`), not the public host. Check ALB idle
  timeout vs tldraw keepalive. *Test: container boot; prod spans after deploy.*
- **A7. Docs** — tabletop SEAMAP progress, README (Modes + SCAFFOLDING callouts),
  root CLAUDE.md layout, notes/AGENT-NOTES.md gotchas.

## Part B — Shuffler integration (parallel with A once F0 lands; only B3's end-to-end verification and prod wiring wait for A5/A6)

- **B0. Feature-owner consultation is mandatory** — library-search /
  two-faced-cards (fleet-scoped after F1) / animations: `-context`, then `-review`
  on the concrete plan, then `-update` after. Known hot spots: the `game.js`
  clipboard hook (animations), Discard's new `WhatHappened` verb (animations),
  sending the current face (two-faced).
- **B1. Prep screen: table name + player name** — two optional inputs on
  `prepare.ejs`; posted through `/start-game`; persisted as optional `tableName` +
  `playerName` on `PersistedGameState` (optional-field exception, **no version
  bump**); `/restart-game` carries both. In table mode the player name is
  load-bearing (it keys the battlefield row) — default to "player" if blank rather
  than block. Game page header shows "at table *name*" linking to `/t/:tableName`
  in a new tab — that link is the spectator-share mechanism. *Test: unit
  persistence; Playwright types both fields, sees the link.*
- **B2. A Tabletop port (fakes, not mocks)** — `src/port-tabletop/`: `TabletopPort`,
  `HttpTabletopGateway` (fetch to `TABLETOP_URL`, auto-instrumented), 
  `FakeTabletopGateway` (records; can be told to fail). Payload per F0; the Shuffler
  mints event `id` per attempt. SCAFFOLDING banner naming the Spine-shaped future.
- **B2a. Mint `cardInstanceId`** — opaque GUID per card in `GameState.newGame`
  (beside `gameCardIndex` assignment); stored on the persisted game card as an
  **optional field, no version bump**: `fromPersistedGameState` mints-on-load when
  missing (in-flight games get ids the next time they're touched). Files:
  `src/GameState.ts`, `src/port-persist-state/types.ts`, `test/generators.ts`.
  *Test: mint-on-load unit test; fake-gateway-never-sees-an-index test (F0).*
- **B3. Play sends the card — send-then-commit** — in `POST /play-card`
  (`apps/shuffler/src/app.ts:1230`), table mode: **send to the table first; only on
  success run `game.playCard()` and persist**; on failure return an error fragment,
  card stays in hand, state untouched (Jess: block the play; the tabletop's
  instanceId no-op covers the worked-but-unacked retry). Solo mode: clipboard flow
  untouched. Button feedback "Sent to table". Zone hint: land → battlefield,
  nonland → stack. *Test: fake fails → error + hand unchanged; Playwright two-app
  flow (verify orchestrates both apps with health-check waits).*
- **B4. Discard** — new hand-modal button + `POST /discard-card/...`; history verb
  "discarded"; card lands in `TableLocation` (graveyard is table geography). Solo
  mode: identical to Play (clipboard) except the verb. Table mode: `zoneHint:
  "graveyard"` (placement: JESS TODO 3). *Test: unit verb + history text; Playwright.*
- **B5. Docs + owners** — CLAUDE.md (routes, TABLETOP_URL), GLOSSARY (Modes), both
  seamaps, feature-owner `-update`s.

## Observability

One trace per played card **request**: browser click → `/play-card` → POST to
tabletop → ingestion span; the trace ends when the request is fulfilled. Cards
persist beyond traces, so nothing durable carries trace context — correlation
after the fact is by `card.instance_id` attribute on spans from every component
(queryable in Honeycomb). WS propagation only at connection establishment. Same
`.be`/`.env`/secret plumbing as the Shuffler; browser spans via the OTLP proxy.

## Risks

1. `room.updateStore` (server-side shape injection) is a young API — verify first
   thing in A1; fallback is a connected "server client." Pin tldraw exactly.
2. ALB + websockets: idle timeout vs tldraw keepalive; second host rule on the
   shared ALB group.
3. Rooms are **in-memory only** — a redeploy wipes the board. Accepted for v0;
   buoy filed for durable reconstruction (Spine log replay for cards; snapshot
   store for doodles).
4. The sync server is supposed to be dumb: it replicates drawings. The card-arrival
   endpoint gives it one domain-ish job — knowing a card was played and where cards
   land. Contained: the endpoint is a stand-in for the Spine's future feed, marked
   SCAFFOLDING, with `// JES-128` markers where contract validation goes, so
   deleting it later is easy.
5. Bypassing the `game.js` clipboard hook touches what the animations owner guards —
   that review is not optional.
6. Send-then-commit means a tabletop outage blocks plays in a joined game —
   JESS TODO 2.

## Follow-up buoys to drop (via seamapping:drop-buoy)

- Durable table reconstruction after restart (low-prio): cards replayable from the
  Spine's event log once it exists; freeform doodles need a tldraw snapshot store.
- Sleeves ("choose your card back / rectangular frame") land with the custom
  CardShape work at Mountain 2 — natural moment, don't pull forward.

## JESS TODO — new open questions from round 1's answers

1. **JESS TODO — interim tableId**: the contract's `tableId` (Spine-minted GUID,
   name as alias) is still marked for your blessing. In the scaffolding, may the
   tabletop registry mint interim `tableId` GUIDs that die with the process, or

2. **JESS TODO — blocked play vs tabletop downtime**: with send-then-commit, a

3. **JESS TODO — where does a Discard land on the canvas?** Stack and battlefield

4. **JESS TODO — player-name collisions** (two "Jess"es at one table): battlefield
   rows are keyed by name now. v0 last-writer-shares-a-row, or disambiguate?
5. **JESS TODO — OTLP proxy**: OK to route browser spans through the tabletop
   server (`POST /otlp/v1/traces`, Honeycomb key stays server-side) rather than
   shipping an ingest key to the page?

## Critical files

- `apps/tabletop/` (new: src/server/{server,rooms,tracing}.ts, src/client/ incl.
  observability/, Dockerfile, k8s/)
- `apps/shuffler/src/GameState.ts` (mint `cardInstanceId` in newGame;
  mint-on-load in fromPersistedGameState)

1	# DESIGN — Event Contract v0 (the fleet's published language)
2	
3	Tracking: [JES-128](https://linear.app/honeycombio/issue/JES-128) · Status: **draft v2, incorporating Jess's first commentary round** (round 1 is in git history)
4	
5	The language-neutral event contract the Spine publishes and both TS apps validate
6	against. Will become JSON Schema in `contracts/` at the repo root; this doc is where
7	we make the decisions first. Leave comments inline — each decision is numbered.
8	
9	Guiding constraints (from SEAMAP.md / the vision doc, as amended by round 1):
10	
11	- One append-only event log per Table. Never replace — supersede.
12	- Visibility on every event. **The shadow is a first-class event**: the private fact
13	  it shadows may never reach the Spine at all (the Shuffler keeps hands and libraries
14	  to itself and sends only the public shadow of what it knows). Visibility marks what
15	  an event reveals, not a derivation chain.
16	- **Provenance and observability are separate.** Provenance is on the event itself —
17	  who initiated it, which app recorded it, when — and is durable. Trace context is
18	  recorded too (super useful for seeing the connections right now) but expires in
19	  60d, so nothing auditable may depend on it. Durable causality between events uses
20	  event `id` references, never trace ids.
21	- Versioned from the start; old data fails loudly. Accepted consequence today: a
22	  deploy can invalidate a Table. If this ever becomes publicly useful, backwards
23	  compatibility must hold for at least the length of a game.
24	- Not all events are game events — see Decision 6 (scope).
25	- **The developer can see the log**: the Spine includes an admin screen (a webapp
26	  component is fine) that shows a table's log human-readably, linking each event to
27	  its trace in Honeycomb. (Scoped into JES-129.)
28	
29	---
30	
31	## Card Identity — an important concept, named
32	
33	How a card is serialized in any event payload, ever:
34	
35	- **Identity is the Scryfall ID.** It captures the exact printing: oracle identity,
36	  all faces, all names (oracle name and the vanity/flavor name), all image URIs.
37	- **Face is card state, not identity** — but it matters at play time (MDFCs are
38	  played as a chosen face), so events about playing/revealing a card carry
39	  `face` alongside identity. The Shuffler already tracks `currentFace`; it must
40	  send it.
41	- Names and image URLs are *derivable conveniences*, not identity, and don't belong
42	  in the contract's card reference. (The pre-Spine Shuffler→Tabletop scaffolding API
43	  may carry an `imageUrl` for rendering without a Scryfall lookup — that's the
44	  scaffolding's business, not the contract's.)
45	
46	**Identity has two levels** (round 2): the *definition* and the *instance*.
47	
48	- **Definition** — `scryfallId`, as above: what kind of card this is.
49	- **Instance** — `cardInstanceId`: *this particular Forest*, the way a physical deck
50	  has one. A GUID minted by the Shuffler, one per card, when the deck becomes a
51	  game's library. Game-mechanically two Forests are equivalent; log-wise they are
52	  distinct individuals, so a single card can be followed through played → tapped →
53	  sacrificed → graveyard, and conservation of cards is checkable: if the table ever
54	  holds more or fewer Forests than the log accounts for, each instance's event
55	  biography shows exactly where. (The Shuffler's internal `gameCardIndex` is the
56	  embryo of this — it *is* static for the life of a game, but it's assigned after
57	  sorting the deck alphabetically (`GameState.newGame`), so an index is the card's
58	  alphabetical rank in a known decklist: **a decodable secret**. It must never cross
59	  the Shuffler's boundary; the contract gets an opaque GUID instead.)
60	- Minting scope — **DECIDED: per game**, at game start (Jess confirmed "this
61	  game"). "Same physical card across game nights" (persisting instance ids into
62	  deck files) is a noted future upgrade, fragile today because deck files are
63	  regenerated from Archidekt/MTGJSON.
64	
65	Contract shape: `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }` + sibling `face` where the event
66	needs it. Downstream consequence: the Tabletop should stamp `instanceId` into each
67	card shape's `meta`, so future physical events (`card.moved`, tap) reference the
68	same individual the game events do.
69	
70	## Decision 1: The envelope — v2, renames from round 1 applied
71	
72	| field | who writes it | what it's for |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `id` | **sender** mints a GUID | idempotency — the Spine elides a retried duplicate |
75	| `tableId` | sender (after learning it) | which table's log. A GUID the **Spine mints at table creation** — the table *name* is a lookup alias, unique only among active tables, living in the `table.created` payload. |
76	| `seq` | **Spine**, on append | authoritative order within the log; senders cannot claim positions |
77	| `name` | sender | the event's kind, namespaced (`card.played`); determines the payload schema. See Decision 6 |
78	| `scope` | sender | what the event affects / how it's perceived — see Decision 6, OPEN |
79	| `acceptedAt` | **Spine**, on append | Spine's clock: when the log accepted it |
80	| `occurredAt` | sender, optional | the initiator app's clock, when physics preceded ingestion |
81	| `initiator` | sender | *who* made this happen: a seat, a named spectator, later the interpreter |
82	| `occurredIn` | sender | *which application* recorded/sent it: `shuffler`, `tabletop`, `spine`, later `interpreter` |
83	| `visibility` | sender | `public` — the only legal value in v0; see Decision 4 |
84	| `traceparent` | sender | W3C trace context — **observability only**, expires with the trace (60d); the admin screen links through it to Honeycomb |
85	| `schemaVersion` | sender | integer version of this `name`'s payload schema |
86	| `payload` | sender | the kind-specific body |
87	
88	**The split in one line:** uniqueness travels with the event (sender GUID);
89	truth-of-order and truth-of-time stay with the log (Spine-assigned `seq`,
90	`acceptedAt`).
91	
92	## Decision 2: The v0 event catalog — OPEN, firming up
93	
94	- `table.created` — payload: table name, creator. Response/log carries the minted `tableId`.
95	- `seat.taken` — payload: seat number (1–4), player name
96	- `card.played` — from the Shuffler (Decision 3: **decided, game event**) —
97	  payload: `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }`, `face`, from which seat, zone hint
98	
99	Near-future, not v0: the Tabletop reporting the *physical* echo (`card.arrived`,
100	scope visible) once it talks to the Spine — mostly ignored by interpretation because
101	it's expected; **interesting precisely when it doesn't arrive**. Also not v0: card
102	movement/tap, chat, interpretation events. Kinds arrive when their producers do.
103	
104	## Decision 3: Game event vs. physical — DECIDED: (a) game event
105	
106	The Shuffler is a deterministic, not-interpreted app: when it plays a card it knows
107	the meaning, so it says so — `card.played`, scope `game`. Physical events are
108	reserved for genuinely observed/ambiguous happenings (the Tabletop's world), and the
109	physical echo of a game event is a separate, expected, low-drama event (see
110	Decision 2). This seeds the log with ground-truth game events for the Interpreter's
111	eval dataset.
112	
113	## Decision 4: Visibility — RESOLVED for v0: everything is `public`
114	
115	Answering round 1's question directly: **no, the Spine does not receive seat-private
116	events in v0** — the Shuffler was never going to send both halves of a pair; it
117	sends only the public shadow of what it privately knows ("seat 2 drew a card",
118	never which card). So v0's enum is exactly `public`, and the pair/shadow mechanics
119	are deferred until a producer actually wants to log a private fact. Envelope
120	future-proofing kept: when shadows arrive, a shadow references the `id` of the event
121	it shadows; adding an enum value is an envelope version bump that old readers reject
122	loudly. (Whether the Spine *ever* holds seat-private facts is a real future
123	decision, not assumed.)
124

128	
129	- Each event `name` versions its payload schema independently (`schemaVersion: 1`

## F — fleet-level steps (first: they unblock A ∥ B parallelism)

- **F0. Freeze the card-arrival payload.** Envelope-lite subset of the contract:
  `{ id, name: "card.played", occurredAt, initiator, card: { scryfallId, instanceId }, face, zoneHint: "stack"|"battlefield"|"graveyard", imageUrl, cardName }`
  (`imageUrl`/`cardName` are blessed scaffolding conveniences, not contract).
  **`gameCardIndex` is forbidden beyond the Shuffler's boundary** — it's the card's
  alphabetical rank in a known decklist, a decodable secret. Record the payload as a
  comment block in `apps/shuffler/src/port-tabletop/types.ts` and in the tabletop
  route, both with `// JES-128` markers; a unit test asserts the fake gateway never
  receives an index.
- **F1. Promote the two-faced-cards owner to fleet scope** (before A5, which renders
  a chosen face). Jess: the complication affects the Spine's events and the Tabletop,
  not just the Shuffler. Restructure `notes/features/two-faced-cards/`: a top-level
  charge ("a card has faces; face is state, not identity") with notes per affected
  component — Shuffler (existing content: `currentFace`, flip), Tabletop (arrival
  renders the played face; future flip gesture), Contract (`face` beside
  `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }`). Update the three `.claude/skills/two-faced-cards-*`
  triggers to fire on tabletop and contract work too. Follow
  `notes/features/HOW-TO-CREATE-A-FEATURE-OWNER.md`.

## Part A — apps/tabletop (parallel with Part B once F0 lands)

- **A1. Scaffold the workspace** — package.json (tldraw, @tldraw/sync{,-core},
  express, ws, react, OTel), tsconfig, vite.config, src/client + src/server; root
  pass-through scripts. **First task: verify server-side shape injection
  (`room.updateStore`) against the pinned tldraw version.** *Test: build compiles,
  vitest smoke.*
- **A2. OTel from the first commit** — server: `src/server/tracing.ts` modeled on
  the Shuffler's (ESM register hook, OTLP http, kube-probe-aware sampler,
  `node --import`). Browser: the `observability/` wrapper module (standard OTel web
  SDK), initialized before mount, `table.name` as a global attribute, exporting to
  our server's OTLP proxy. `run` script + `.env` pattern (`.be` before `.env` — same
  trap). *Test: spans in Honeycomb env `local`, datasets `mtg-tabletop` /
  `mtg-tabletop-web`.*
- **A3. Sync server + room registry (scaffolding)** — `rooms.ts` per the registry
  row; Express + ws upgrade at `/connect/:roomSlug`; `traceparent` accepted on the
  connection URL (propagation belongs to the connection *request* only); SPA
  fallback for `/t/*`; `/health`; one shared slugify. Rooms are **in-memory only**,
  ephemeral, accepted for v0. `table.id` + `table.name` on spans; room lifecycle
  (created/emptied/evicted) as span events. *Test: vitest, real server on an
  ephemeral port, two ws clients share a room.*
- **A4. The `/t/:tableName` page** — `/` landing takes a table name only (player
  name is a Shuffler-prep concern); `/t/:tableName` renders `<Tldraw>` with
  `useSync`. Spectators come free: anyone with the URL joins. Square corners,
  tablet-friendly targets. *Test: Playwright, two contexts, draw in one, see it in
  the other; a tabletop `verify.sh` mirroring the Shuffler's.*
- **A5. Card-arrival API — the seam the Spine absorbs** — `POST
  /api/tables/:tableName/cards`, payload per F0. Dedup on `id` **and** on
  `instanceId` already present (no-op). **Arrival layout (regions, v0-minimal)**:
  a fixed **Stack area**, plus a **battlefield row per player** keyed by
  `initiator`, allocated in first-play order — Jess: lands arrive in the player's
  battlefield, everything else on the stack. The Shuffler picks the `zoneHint`
  (it knows land vs nonland from `cardTypes`); the tabletop stays meaning-free and
  honors coordinates. Graveyard placement: JESS TODO 3. `shape.meta` =
  `{ instanceId, scryfallId, cardName }`. Ingestion span attrs: `card.instance_id`,
  `card.scryfall_id`, `card.name`, `event.id`, `table.name`, `zone.hint`; the
  client store-listener emits a standalone "card arrived on canvas" span correlated
  by `card.instance_id` (not propagation — the play trace ends when the ingestion
  request is fulfilled). SCAFFOLDING banner naming the future: Shuffler emits
  `card.played` to the Spine; Tabletop subscribes to the table's public feed.
  *Test: vitest POST + both dedup paths; Playwright: a land and a nonland arrive
  in different areas.*
- **A6. Docker, k8s, deploy** — Dockerfile with repo root as build context; `k8s/`:
  deployment (`mtg-tabletop`, key from `mtg-deck-shuffler-secret`), service,
  ingress on ALB group `only-one-alb-please`, host **`table.jessitron.honeydemo.io`**
  (decided: subdomain — easiest, copies the Shuffler's external-dns + TLS host
  block, spares Vite base-path and ws-path juggling). The Shuffler's server-side
  POST uses in-cluster DNS (`TABLETOP_URL=http://mtg-tabletop-service`), not the
  public host. Check ALB idle timeout vs tldraw keepalive. *Test: container boot;
  prod spans after deploy.*
- **A7. Docs** — tabletop SEAMAP progress, README (Modes + SCAFFOLDING callouts),
  root CLAUDE.md layout, notes/AGENT-NOTES.md gotchas.

## Part B — Shuffler integration (parallel with A once F0 lands; only B3's end-to-end verification and prod wiring wait for A5/A6)

- **B0. Feature-owner consultation is mandatory** — library-search /
  two-faced-cards (fleet-scoped, after F1) / animations: `-context`, `-review` on
  the concrete plan, `-update` after. Known hot spots: the `game.js` clipboard hook
  (animations), Discard's new `WhatHappened` verb (animations), sending the played
  face (two-faced).
- **B1. Prep screen: table name + player name** — two optional inputs on
  `prepare.ejs` (Jess: a player also wants to type their name when joining);
  posted through `/start-game`; persisted as optional `tableName` + `playerName`
  on `PersistedGameState` (optional-field exception, **no version bump**);
  `/restart-game` carries both. Player name is load-bearing in table mode (it keys
  the battlefield row) — default to "player" if blank rather than block. Game page
  header shows "at table *name*" linking to `/t/:tableName` in a new tab — that
  link is also the spectator-share mechanism (Jess: yes please). *Test: unit
  persistence; Playwright types both fields, sees the link.*
- **B2. A Tabletop port (fakes, not mocks)** — `src/port-tabletop/`: `TabletopPort`,
  `HttpTabletopGateway` (fetch to `TABLETOP_URL`, auto-instrumented so trace
  context propagates free), `FakeTabletopGateway` (records; can be told to fail).
  Payload per F0; the Shuffler mints a fresh event `id` per attempt. SCAFFOLDING
  banner naming the Spine-shaped future (Jess: surprised it's direct
  Shuffler→Tabletop, expected Spine — OK for now, breaks the dependency, change
  later).
- **B2a. Mint `cardInstanceId`** — opaque GUID per card in `GameState.newGame`
  (beside `gameCardIndex` assignment); stored on the persisted game card as an
  **optional field, no version bump**: `fromPersistedGameState` **mints-on-load**
  when missing, so in-flight games get ids the next time they're touched. Files:
  `src/GameState.ts`, `src/port-persist-state/types.ts`, `test/generators.ts`.
  *Test: mint-on-load unit test; the F0 no-index test.*
- **B3. Play sends the card — send-then-commit** — in `POST /play-card`
  (`apps/shuffler/src/app.ts:1230`), table mode: **send to the table first; only
  on success run `game.playCard()` and persist**; on failure return an error
  fragment — the card stays in hand, game state untouched (Jess: block the play;
  a play that silently missed the tabletop is worse than one that says it failed;
  the tabletop's `instanceId` no-op covers worked-but-unacked). Solo mode:
  clipboard flow exactly as today (Mural workflow unbroken — joining a table is
  optional). Button feedback "Sent to table". Zone hint: land → battlefield,
  nonland → stack. *Test: fake fails → error + hand unchanged; Playwright two-app
  flow (verify orchestrates both apps with health-check waits).*
- **B4. Discard** — new hand-modal button + `POST /discard-card/...`; history verb
  "discarded"; card lands in `TableLocation` (graveyard is table geography, not
  Shuffler state). Solo mode: identical to Play except the verb (Jess: yes, same
  as Play). Table mode: `zoneHint: "graveyard"` — placement JESS TODO 3. *Test:
  unit verb + history text; Playwright.*
- **B5. Docs + owners** — CLAUDE.md (routes, TABLETOP_URL), GLOSSARY (Modes), both
  seamaps, feature-owner `-update`s.

## Observability

One trace per played-card **request**: browser click → `/play-card` → POST to
tabletop → ingestion span; the trace ends when the request is fulfilled. Cards
persist beyond traces, so nothing durable carries trace context — after-the-fact
correlation is by `card.instance_id` attribute on spans from every component
(queryable in Honeycomb). WS propagation only at connection establishment. Same
`.be`/`.env`/secret plumbing as the Shuffler; browser spans via the OTLP proxy.

## Risks

1. `room.updateStore` (server-side shape injection) is a young API — verify first
   thing in A1; fallback is a connected "server client." Pin tldraw exactly.
2. ALB + websockets: idle timeout vs tldraw keepalive; second host rule on the
   shared ALB group.
3. Rooms are **in-memory only** — a redeploy wipes the board. Accepted for v0
   (fine for intentional redeploys); buoy filed for durable reconstruction.
4. In plain words: the sync server is supposed to be dumb — it replicates
   drawings. The card-arrival endpoint gives it one domain-ish job (knowing a card
   was played, and where cards land). We keep that contained: the endpoint is
   written as a stand-in for the Spine's future feed, marked SCAFFOLDING, with
   `// JES-128` markers where contract validation goes, so deleting it later is
   easy.
5. Bypassing the `game.js` clipboard hook touches what the animations owner
   guards — that review is not optional.
6. Send-then-commit means a tabletop outage blocks plays in a joined game —
   JESS TODO 2.

## Buoys to drop (via seamapping:drop-buoy, low priority)

- Reconstruct a table after restart: card locations replayable from the Spine's
  event log once it exists; freeform doodles need a tldraw snapshot store.
- "Choose your sleeves" (rectangular card frames, custom backs) lands with the
  custom CardShape work at Mountain 2 — the natural moment; a sleeve image is
  exactly what a face-down card back needs.

## JESS TODO — new questions your answers surfaced

1. **JESS TODO — interim tableId in the scaffolding**: the contract has the Spine
   minting `tableId`. Until the Spine exists, may the tabletop's registry mint
   interim GUIDs that die with the process, or does v0 run name-only?
2. **JESS TODO — blocked play vs tabletop downtime**: with send-then-commit, a
   tabletop outage makes a joined game unplayable mid-game. Acceptable for v0, or
   should the game page get a "leave table / go solo" control?
3. **JESS TODO — where does a Discard land on the canvas?** Stack and battlefield
   are defined. Proposal: a per-player graveyard spot at the end of that player's
   battlefield row.
4. **JESS TODO — player-name collisions** (two "Jess"es at one table): battlefield
   rows are keyed by player name now. v0 last-writer-shares-a-row, or
   disambiguate with a suffix?
5. **JESS TODO — OTLP proxy for browser spans**: OK to route them through the
   tabletop server (`POST /otlp/v1/traces`, Honeycomb key stays server-side),
   rather than shipping an ingest key to the page?

## Critical files

- `apps/tabletop/` (new: src/server/{server,rooms,tracing}.ts, src/client/ incl.
  `observability/`, Dockerfile, k8s/)
- `apps/shuffler/src/GameState.ts` (mint `cardInstanceId` in newGame;
  mint-on-load in fromPersistedGameState)
- `apps/shuffler/src/app.ts` (`/play-card` send-then-commit; `/start-game`
  tableName+playerName; new `/discard-card`)
- `apps/shuffler/src/port-persist-state/types.ts` (optional `cardInstanceId`,
  `tableName`, `playerName` — no version bump)
- `apps/shuffler/src/port-tabletop/` (new port; F0 payload comment block)
- `apps/shuffler/public/game.js` (clipboard hook: skip in table mode)
- `apps/shuffler/views/prepare.ejs` (table + player name inputs)
- `notes/features/two-faced-cards/` (F1 fleet-scoping)

🥕🪄 Plan v2 is committed (`c40c0d4`; your commented round-1 lives at `56fe5b3`). The planner accepted almost everything; here's the shape of it:

**Big structural changes from your comments:**
- **"Why serial?" — you won, mostly.** New fleet-level step **F0 freezes the card-arrival payload** (an envelope-lite subset of the contract, `gameCardIndex` explicitly forbidden); once that's frozen, Parts A and B run in parallel — only B3's end-to-end verification and prod wiring wait for the tabletop to exist.
- **Traceparent is off the card.** Your framing went straight in: traces follow requests until fulfilled; cards persist. `shape.meta` = `{ instanceId, scryfallId, cardName }`, and after-the-fact correlation is by `card.instance_id` span attribute — which is exactly your card-in-deck ID earning its keep in observability too.
- **Send-then-commit**: block the play on failure; the card stays in hand. The tabletop treats a re-arriving `instanceId` as a no-op — one instance exists once — covering the worked-but-unacked case you called out.
- **Regions**: stack area + per-player battlefield row keyed by the player name, which is why B1 now has a **player name input** next to the table name (both persisted, no version bump).
- **F1 promotes the two-faced-cards owner to fleet scope** — top-level charge, notes per component (Shuffler, Tabletop, Contract) — before A5 renders a chosen face.
- **Modes are now a named section**: solo (clipboard, unchanged) / at a table / spectating.
- Decided per your answers: subdomain `table.jessitron.honeydemo.io`, standard OTel web SDK in our own wrapper module, Vitest, ephemeral rooms, table-name link on the game page.

**Two gentle pushbacks the planner made** (I agree with both): sleeves don't need to come sooner — rectangularity only matters when a custom CardShape draws its own frame at Mountain 2, and that's also when a sleeve image is exactly what a face-down back needs (buoy, not acceleration); and rooms-die-on-redeploy stays accepted with your reconstruct-someday buoy noted.

**Five new JESS TODOs** your answers surfaced, at `notes/PLAN-tabletop-v0.md:187`: interim `tableId` minting in the scaffolding, blocked-play vs. tabletop downtime (want a "go solo" escape hatch?), where Discards land on canvas, player-name collisions (rows are keyed by name now), and blessing the OTLP proxy for browser spans.

🥕🪄 That closes the last open decision — **the contract doc now has all six decisions DECIDED** (committed through `5d629a7`):

1. Envelope — sender GUID `id`, Spine-minted `seq`/`acceptedAt`/`tableId`, `initiator`+`occurredIn`, `schemaVersion`, `traceparent` demoted to observability
2. Catalog — `table.created`, `seat.taken`, `card.played` (with `card.picked_up` and the shadow events noted as near-future, per your comment — same pipe, cheap once the first one flows)
3. `card.played` is a game event
4. Visibility — all `public` in v0; shadows are first-class when they arrive
5. Versioning — per-name payload schemas + one envelope version, fail loudly
6. `scope` — off, until real filtering needs teach us the values; `name`-prefix filtering suffices at three kinds

Plus the named concepts: Card Identity (definition `scryfallId` / instance `cardInstanceId`, per-game, opaque because `gameCardIndex` is a decodable secret).

**Where that leaves the lanes:**
- **JES-128's remaining work is mechanical**: turn this doc into actual JSON Schema files in `contracts/` (envelope + three payload schemas). I can do that now — it's an hour of translation, not new decisions.
- **JES-129 (Spine walking skeleton) is unblocked** — its start condition was "contract sketch exists," and it now has more than a sketch. Ready to kick off as a parallel agent session whenever you say.
- **The Tabletop plan** waits only on its 5 JESS TODOs (`notes/PLAN-tabletop-v0.md:187`) — interim tableId, downtime escape hatch, Discard placement, name collisions, OTLP proxy.

Want me to write the `contracts/` schemas while you knock down those 5?

## Round-2 answers — DECIDED (apply these over the plan body)

1. **Registry is name-only in v0** — no interim `tableId` GUIDs; v0 doesn't wait on
   the Spine. (Delete the `tableId` half of the registry row.)
2. **Tabletop downtime blocking plays is acceptable.** And: **the Prep object
   records all needed Table info** (table name, player name, seat id) — the Prep
   page is where the Shuffler joins a table, and that record is what enables
   rejoining later. So B1 persists onto `PersistedGamePrep` as well as
   `PersistedGameState` (both optional fields, no version bumps).
3. **Canvas regions per player**: battlefield row + a **Graveyard spot** and a
   **smaller Exile spot** at the end of it. Discard → graveyard spot.
4. **Player names are not unique — seats get their own IDs.** The Shuffler mints a
   short GUID `seatId` at prep/join time (a sequence once the Spine owns seats);
   battlefield rows are keyed by `seatId`, labeled with the player name. F0's
   payload changes: `initiator` becomes `{ seatId, playerName }`. The contract's
   `seat.taken` payload now carries `seatId` too.
5. **Browser spans route to an OpenTelemetry Collector**, not a proxy endpoint in
   the tabletop server and not a key in the page. Collectors already run in the
   cluster — find one (or stand one up in `apps/tabletop/k8s/`) with an
   OTLP-http receiver + CORS for the tabletop origin; locally, a collector config
   in the repo or fall back to the server-side key only for `local` env.

Build the Spine walking skeleton (Linear JES-129) in /Users/jessitron/code/jessitron/mtg-deck-shuffler. The Spine is a new Ruby service in services/spine/. Read first: services/spine/SEAMAP.md (North Star, Mountains 1–2, Safe Harbor, enabling constraints), notes/DESIGN-event-contract-v0.md (ALL SIX decisions are settled — this is your contract), notes/DESIGN-the-table-vision.md, root SEAMAP.md, and root CLAUDE.md (working agreements).

Scope, in order:

1. **Write the contract schemas (JES-128's mechanical remainder)**: JSON Schema files in `contracts/` at the repo root — one envelope schema (fields per the contract doc's Decision 1: id, tableId, seq, name, acceptedAt, occurredAt, initiator, occurredIn, visibility, traceparent, schemaVersion, payload; no scope field) and three payload schemas: table.created, seat.taken (seatId short GUID + seat number 1–4 + display player name), card.played (card: { scryfallId, instanceId }, face, seat, zoneHint). Language-neutral, versioned (envelope version + per-name schemaVersion). Include a README explaining the fail-loudly rule and that both Ruby and TS sides validate on receipt.

2. **The Ruby service**: tables you can create and join by name (Spine mints the tableId GUID at creation; the name is a lookup alias unique among active tables); seats 1–4 with seatIds; spectators need nothing; an append-only event log per table that ingests contract events (validate against contracts/ on receipt, fail loudly on unknown name/version; dedup on sender event id; Spine assigns seq and acceptedAt). Plain domain code — the Journeys pattern belongs to the future Interpreter component, NOT this skeleton. However, choose the stack with the Interpreter's future in mind: the Journeys framework (see services/spine/interpreter/docs/journeys/) is Rails/ActiveRecord-flavored (Briefasaurus::ActiveRecordJourney), so default to Rails unless you find a strong reason otherwise; SQLite for storage matches the fleet's pattern (the Shuffler uses SQLite + a PVC in k8s).

3. **The admin screen**: a webapp page in the Spine showing a table's event log human-readably — the developer follows along in real time-ish (poll or refresh is fine for v0) — with each event linking to its trace in Honeycomb (build the trace URL from the recorded traceparent; team "modernity", env "mtg-deck-shuffler" in prod, "local" locally).

4. **Observability from the FIRST commit**: OpenTelemetry Ruby SDK exporting OTLP to Honeycomb; accept inbound W3C trace context on the ingestion endpoint; interesting attributes on spans (table.id, table.name, event.name, event.id, card.instance_id where present). `.be` at the repo root holds HONEYCOMB_API_KEY; it must be sourced BEFORE any .env that interpolates it into OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (see how apps/shuffler/verify.sh and its .env do it — mirror the pattern with a `run` script for the spine).

5. **Tests**: no mocks — fakes only (repo-wide rule). RSpec or minitest, your call. Domain tests for table/seat/log invariants (append-only, seq monotonic per table, dedup on event id, loud failure on bad schema/version), request tests for ingestion and the admin screen.

6. **Deploy**: Dockerfile (repo root as build context if it needs the workspace, otherwise self-contained is fine for Ruby) + k8s manifests modeled on apps/shuffler/k8s/ (same cluster, ALB group only-one-alb-please, hostname suggestion spine.jessitron.honeydemo.io, reuse mtg-deck-shuffler-secret for the Honeycomb key, PVC for SQLite like the Shuffler's). Attempt the deploy with the same tooling apps/shuffler/deploy.sh uses; if cluster access fails from your session, commit everything and report deploy as the remaining manual step.

Working agreements: commit after each conceptual change, tagged "- claude". IMPORTANT — another agent is concurrently working in this same checkout on apps/tabletop/ and apps/shuffler/: stage ONLY your own files with explicit `git add <paths>` (never `git add -A` or `git commit -a`), commit immediately after staging, and on an index.lock conflict wait 2 seconds and retry. Do not push. You own services/spine/ and contracts/; do not touch apps/. Pick a local port that clashes with nothing (Shuffler tests use 3344; tabletop ~5180; use e.g. 4600). Update services/spine/SEAMAP.md and root CLAUDE.md's repo notes when done.

Final report: what runs (with test evidence), the contracts/ files written, admin-screen screenshot-level description, deployed vs pending, commits made, and any contract ambiguities you hit (do NOT change the contract doc — report ambiguities instead).

## Summary

Pressing ctrl-C to cancel text being typed in the prompt also stops a running background agent — and a user-stopped background agent can then never be resumed, even when the stop was accidental. This cost us a long-running implementation agent twice in one session.

## What happened

1. A background agent (launched via the Agent tool with `run_in_background: true`) was mid-task.
2. The user was typing a message in the Claude Code prompt, decided to discard it, and pressed **ctrl-C intending only to clear the input buffer**.
3. Claude Code stopped the background agent instead ("Background agent ... was stopped by the user").
4. When the main conversation tried to resume it with SendMessage, the runtime refused: *"Agent ... was stopped by the user and won't be resumed. Treat its work as cancelled; only launch a new agent if the user explicitly asks."*
5. This happened **twice in the same session** (the first time to a planning agent, the second to an implementation agent partway through a multi-step task). The only recovery was launching a brand-new agent with instructions to re-assess repo state and continue — burning tokens and time re-establishing context.

## Expected behavior

- ctrl-C while there is text in the input buffer should only clear the buffer (its long-standing terminal meaning of "abandon current line"), never touch background work.
- Stopping a background agent should require a deliberate, unambiguous gesture (or a confirmation when the agent is mid-task).
- A user-stopped agent should be resumable — the transcript exists; SendMessage already resumes *completed* agents from their transcripts. Accidental stops are common enough that "stopped by user" should not be a terminal, unrecoverable state.

## Environment

- Claude Code CLI on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), iTerm2
- Model: claude-fable-5

Don't inline your own URL construction anywhere — this function is the one door.
- `face` is a sibling of `card: { scryfallId, instanceId }`, never part of the card reference. The contract schema (`contracts/payloads/card.played.v1.json`) requires `face: enum ["front","back"]` — your payload already matches. If you ever feel a need to change that shape, it's a schemaVersion bump (new v2 file), not an edit.

**Discard of a flipped card:** discard should send the CURRENT face, same as play — a flipped MDFC goes to the graveyard as the face it was. Note `GameState.mulligan()` resets `currentFace` to `"front"` when a card returns to library; discard moves to `TableLocation`, which does NOT reset the face — that's correct, don't add a reset. Mint-on-load in `fromPersistedGameState` must persist on next save so the instance id is stable (the Tabletop dedups on `instanceId`; a changing id would defeat the retried-play no-op).

# Final Report — Tabletop v0 Part B (JES-127), Shuffler integration

## Already done before I started (not redone)
- **F0** (`8e00bb4`): frozen card-arrival payload as a `// JES-128` comment block in `apps/shuffler/src/port-tabletop/types.ts`, incl. `TabletopPort` interface, `buildCardPlayedEvent`, and the payload-level no-index test.
- **F1** (`7e2d0d6`): two-faced-cards owner promoted to fleet scope.
- **Part A complete** (A1–A6) and deployed at table.jessitron.honeydemo.io — I ran the real two-app flow locally.

## What I did (commits, each with verify-first failing tests)
- **B0 consultations**: `library-search-context`, `two-faced-cards-context`, `animations-context` — all guidance absorbed (mint-on-load durable, `gameCardIndex` untouched internally, current face on discard with no face reset, distinct button class instead of branching in the clipboard hook, no new `WhatHappened` shapes).
- **B2a** (`8ad52b9`): `cardInstanceId` GUID per card — minted in `GameState.newGame`, mint-on-load in `fromPersistedGameState` (durable on next save, so the Tabletop's instanceId dedup holds), threaded through `hydration.ts`; optional fields, **no version bumps**. `test/GameState-cardInstanceId.test.ts`.
- **B1** (`e1b4343`): prep screen table-name + player-name inputs (square corners, prefilled for rejoin); `/start-game` mints the short-GUID `seatId` at join and records table info on **both** `PersistedGamePrep` (both adapters' explicit `retrievePrep` field lists extended) and `PersistedGameState`; player name defaults to "player" rather than blocking; `/restart-game` carries everything forward; game page "at table _name_" link (`TABLETOP_PUBLIC_URL`, default table.jessitron.honeydemo.io, new tab, HTML-escaped) — the spectator-share URL. Unit + 3 Playwright tests.
- **B2** (`eaeba84`): `HttpTabletopGateway` (fetch to `TABLETOP_URL`, default `http://localhost:5180`, prod in-cluster DNS; auto-instrumented; throws on non-2xx) and `FakeTabletopGateway` (records; can be told to fail); wired via new optional `tabletopPort` param on `createApp`; SCAFFOLDING banners naming the Spine-shaped future. **Gateway-level no-index test** (F0's fake-gateway assertion) in `test/port-tabletop/gateways.test.ts` — real ephemeral HTTP server, no mocks.
- **B3** (`a8aa418`): send-then-commit in `POST /play-card` — table mode sends FIRST (`sendToTable.ts`: fresh event id per attempt; land→battlefield, nonland→stack from `cardTypes`); only on success `playCard()`+persist; failure → 502 error modal, card stays in hand, no event recorded. Solo clipboard flow byte-identical (table buttons get `table-play-button`, so the `play-button` hook never fires). "Sent to table" optimistic button feedback in game.js. Applied the Part A handoff: card modal always closes, `#modal-container` closes only on `event.detail.successful` — which required `{code:"502", swap:true, error:true}` in htmx `responseHandling` (**without `error:true` htmx reports success and the error modal self-destructs** — caught by the Playwright failure-path test).
- **B4** (`65b8df4`): `GameState.discardCard` (Hand→`TableLocation`, keeps `currentFace`), `MoveCardEvent` gains optional `verb: "discard"` (old events valid), history renders "Discard: card" via `nameMoveCardEvent`, undo works; `POST /discard-card` mirrors play's send-then-commit with zoneHint `"graveyard"`; hand-modal Discard button (solo = clipboard like Play). 5 unit + Playwright tests.
- **Two-app verification** (`ba96525`): `verify-tabletop-integration.spec.ts` spawns the real tabletop from `apps/tabletop/dist` on 5180, plays + discards through the Shuffler UI, and a spectator page sees both cards arrive on the tldraw canvas. **Passing — nothing pending Part A.** (Skips with a build hint if the tabletop isn't built.)
- **B5** (`aeadc65` + three owner commits): root CLAUDE.md (Table Mode section: routes, env vars, identity rule), GLOSSARY (Seat ID, Solo/Table Mode, Discard — small edits), shuffler README (Modes + SCAFFOLDING) and SEAMAP (Mountain 2 peaks reached); `animations-update` (incl. fixing the stale `.being-played`/`swap:1.5s` checklist items per handoff), `two-faced-cards-update`, `library-search-update`.

## Test evidence
- Unit: **210 tests, 27 suites, all green** (jest).
- Playwright: **46 specs green** across full `verify.sh` runs, including the new table-mode (3), discard (1), and two-app (1) specs; the failure path is exercised for real (tabletop down → play blocked, hand unchanged).

## Boundary with Part A
Untouched: `apps/tabletop/`, `services/spine/`, `contracts/`. I only *run* the tabletop's built dist in the two-app spec. Nothing left pending.

## Deviations / notes for Jess
1. **History verb reads "Discard: <card>"** (imperative, matching "Play"/"Draw"), not literally "discarded" — consistency with existing history style.
2. **No supertest-style route test**: `src/app.ts` uses `import.meta`, which this jest setup can't compile (repo convention: app.ts is never unit-imported). The send-then-commit logic lives in testable `sendToTable.ts` (unit, fakes) and the route behavior is covered end-to-end by Playwright (both failure and success paths).
3. **Flake found & handled**: Playwright-speed clicks on a freshly-opened card modal can straddle htmx swap/settle (mousedown/mouseup on different nodes → click swallowed; impossible at human speed). Specs use a retry-`toPass` pattern; documented in the animations owner's knowledge base.
4. Shared checkout worked fine — explicit-path staging only; two other-agent commits interleaved cleanly.</result>

#!/bin/bash

port_override=$PORT

source .env

# port_override if defined, otherwise $PORT as defined in .env
APP_PORT=${port_override:-${PORT}}

# Announce readiness once the app answers, so you (or a script) don't have to poll
# by hand. Runs alongside npm start, which stays in the foreground as usual.
(
  for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    if curl -s "http://localhost:$APP_PORT/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "──────────────────────────────────────────────"
      echo "✅ app ready          http://localhost:$APP_PORT/"
      echo "──────────────────────────────────────────────"
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.5
  done
) &

PORT=$APP_PORT npm start

#!/bin/bash
# Run the Spine locally, with telemetry to Honeycomb.
#
# Source .be BEFORE .env: .env's OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS interpolates
# $HONEYCOMB_API_KEY at source time, and that key is defined in .be at the repo
# root. Wrong order (or no .be) => telemetry silently 401s ("unknown API key").
# Same pattern as apps/shuffler/verify.sh.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

port_override=$PORT

REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo ../..)"
for candidate in .be "$REPO_ROOT/.be"; do
    if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then
        source "$candidate"
        break
    fi
done
source .env

APP_PORT=${port_override:-${PORT}}

# Announce readiness once the app answers.
(
  for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    if curl -s "http://localhost:$APP_PORT/up" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "──────────────────────────────────────────────"
      echo "✅ spine ready        http://localhost:$APP_PORT/admin/tables"
      echo "──────────────────────────────────────────────"
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.5
  done
) &

PORT=$APP_PORT bundle exec rails server -p "$APP_PORT"

#!/bin/bash
# Run the whole fleet locally: Spine, Tabletop, and Shuffler.
#
#   ./run                 all three, default ports
#   SHUFFLER_PORT=3355 ./run    override any port
#
# Ports: Shuffler 3344, Tabletop 5180, Spine 4600 (defaults; each overridable).
# Ctrl-C stops everything.
#
# Telemetry: .be (repo root) is sourced here, BEFORE each app's run script
# sources its own .env — the .envs interpolate $HONEYCOMB_API_KEY at source
# time, so the key must already be in the environment. Local spans go to
# Honeycomb env `local`.

set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

if [ -f .be ]; then
  source .be
else
  echo "⚠️  no .be at repo root — telemetry will 401 (app still runs)"
fi

SHUFFLER_PORT=${SHUFFLER_PORT:-3344}
TABLETOP_PORT=${TABLETOP_PORT:-5180}
SPINE_PORT=${SPINE_PORT:-4600}

# The Shuffler talks to the local Tabletop, and its "at table" link points there too.
export TABLETOP_URL="http://localhost:$TABLETOP_PORT"
export TABLETOP_PUBLIC_URL="http://localhost:$TABLETOP_PORT"

prefix() {
  local label="$1"
  while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s %s\n' "$label" "$line"; done
}

PIDS=()

start() {
  local label="$1" dir="$2" port="$3"
  (cd "$dir" && PORT="$port" ./run 2>&1 | prefix "$label") &
  PIDS+=($!)
}

cleanup() {
  echo ""
  echo "⚓ furling sails — stopping the fleet..."
  # Kill everything this script started (children inherit our process group).
  kill "${PIDS[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true
  pkill -P $$ 2>/dev/null || true
  wait 2>/dev/null
}
trap cleanup INT TERM EXIT

echo "⛵ launching the fleet: spine :$SPINE_PORT · tabletop :$TABLETOP_PORT · shuffler :$SHUFFLER_PORT"
start "[spine   ]" services/spine "$SPINE_PORT"
start "[tabletop]" apps/tabletop  "$TABLETOP_PORT"
start "[shuffler]" apps/shuffler  "$SHUFFLER_PORT"

# One combined readiness banner once all three answer.
(
  ok=0
  for _ in $(seq 1 240); do
    s=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://localhost:$SPINE_PORT/up" 2>/dev/null || true)
    t=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://localhost:$TABLETOP_PORT/health" 2>/dev/null || true)
    h=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://localhost:$SHUFFLER_PORT/health" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$s" = "200" ] && [ "$t" = "200" ] && [ "$h" = "200" ]; then
      echo "══════════════════════════════════════════════════"
      echo "⛵ the fleet is afloat"
      echo "   shuffler   http://localhost:$SHUFFLER_PORT/"
      echo "   tabletop   http://localhost:$TABLETOP_PORT/         (tables at /t/<name>)"
      echo "   spine      http://localhost:$SPINE_PORT/admin/tables"
      echo "══════════════════════════════════════════════════"
      ok=1
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.5
  done
  [ "$ok" = "1" ] || echo "⚠️  fleet not fully up after 120s — check the logs above"
) &

wait

content.text:
🥕🪄 Done — **`./run` from the repo root now launches the whole fleet** (committed as `1672984`, tested end to end):

```
⛵ launching the fleet: spine :4600 · tabletop :5180 · shuffler :3344
...
══════════════════════════════════════════════════
⛵ the fleet is afloat
   shuffler   http://localhost:3344/
   tabletop   http://localhost:5180/         (tables at /t/<name>)
   spine      http://localhost:4600/admin/tables
══════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

What it does: starts each app via its own existing `run` script with prefixed logs (`[spine ]`, `[tabletop]`, `[shuffler]`), sources `.be` once at the top so all three get telemetry to Honeycomb env `local`, and wires the Shuffler to the local tabletop (`TABLETOP_URL`/`TABLETOP_PUBLIC_URL` point at :5180, so the "at table" link works locally). Ctrl-C furls all sails — teardown kills the whole process tree, which I verified frees every port. Ports override via `SHUFFLER_PORT`/`TABLETOP_PORT`/`SPINE_PORT`.

I went with processes over Docker Compose deliberately: your per-app `run` scripts already handle the `.be`-before-`.env` telemetry dance, and native processes mean a code change is just a restart, not an image rebuild. If you later want the compose version (say, to test the actual containers), that's a separate artifact worth its own moment — the Dockerfiles all exist now, so it'd be cheap.

Verified in the test run: all three healthy, and a `card.played` POST to the local tabletop landed with a 201. It's in CLAUDE.md under Development Commands.
